text: This is the disaster-recovery backbone for PolicyClaimsDB, the most important lesson in this phase.

A secondary server in a different Azure region, Active Geo-Replication keeping it continuously in sync, and an auto-failover group, thornridge-sql-failover-group, wrapping both behind one stable listener endpoint.
The failover group is created with an automatic failover policy and a one-hour grace period, so a real regional outage triggers failover without a 2am phone call.

The Azure-side configuration here is correct and complete. What it cannot verify is whether the claims-processing app's own connection string actually points at the listener, rather than the primary server directly -- that's the app team's to confirm, or a real failover test to prove.
The database side of disaster recovery is built and verified. Next: establishing a performance baseline with Query Store.
